question: In case of a moderately skewed frequency distribution, the mean is 50 and the median is 53. If the coefficient of variation is 20%. then the coefficient of skewness is:
solution:
The correct answer is** -0.9**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** Coefficient of Skewness:

__
 
• The coefficient of skewness is calculated using the formula:
 
• {Skewness} = frac{3({Mean} - {Median})}{{Standard Deviation}} 
 
• Given:
 
 
• Mean (μ) = 50
 
• Median = 53
 
• Coefficient of Variation (CV) = 20% = 0.20
 
 
 
• Standard Deviation (σ) can be calculated as:
 
• sigma = {CV} times mu = 0.20 times 50 = 10 
 
• Now, calculate skewness:
 
• {Skewness} = (3(50 - 53))/(10) = (3(-3))/(10) = -0.9 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 Explanation of Options:

 
• **Option 1) 0.6:**

 
 
• This option assumes a positive skewness which is incorrect.
 
• The formula and given values lead to a negative skewness.
 
• 0.6 is not the correct result from the formula used.
 
 
 
• **Option 2) 0.8:**
 
 
• This option also assumes a positive skewness which is incorrect.
 
• The correct calculation results in a negative value.
 
• 0.8 is not derived from the given values and formula.
 
 
 
• **Option 3) -0.9:**
 
 
• This is the correct option based on the given data.
 
• It correctly reflects the negative skewness derived from the formula.
 
• All given values fit accurately into the skewness formula.
 
 
 
• **Option 4) 0.5:**
 
 
• This option assumes a positive skewness which is incorrect.
 
• It does not match the calculated value from the given data.
 
• 0.5 does not fit the formula with the provided mean, median, and standard deviation.
